evidence: pull-service.lisp:308-314: (handler-case (multiple-value-bind (user pass) (fnn-feed-auth-profile (list :authinfo path nil)) (list user pass)) (error () (fnn-err "pull: the credential profile of peer ~a is unreadable" ...) nil))
failure-message: cleanup OS error must preserve primary store fault
fix: Catch only fnn-feed-auth-error and fnn-os-error here, and let fnn-store-fault and its subclasses propagate to the worker guard.
reviewer: pull-service.lisp:308-316 wraps fnn-feed-auth-profile in (handler-case ... (error () ... nil)). fnn-store-fault and fnn-entry-guard-fault (io.lisp:77, 89) are subclasses of error, so an ACL2 fault from fn-owner-feed-profile-max-octets or fn-owner-feed-profile-decode becomes an 'unreadable profile' log line and a refused begin. The push feed's own caller does not do this: it catches only fnn-feed-auth-error and OS errors (feed-service.lisp:428-429). It is reachable only through a host/ACL2 contract break, so the severity is low.
scenario: fnn-feed-auth-profile calls (fnn-core 'fn-owner-feed-profile-decode ...) and (fnn-core 'fn-owner-feed-profile-max-octets). A guard violation or core fault there (fnn-entry-guard-fault or fnn-store-fault, both subclasses of error) is caught and reported as an unreadable profile, and the round goes on as a refused begin. A host/ACL2 contract break, which should stop the owner as exit 4, becomes a routine per-round log line that repeats every interval.
title: fnn-pull-profile swallows every error, including ACL2 faults, as an unreadable credential
